message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10⁴³**.  

This figure is commonly referred to as the *Shannon number* (after Claude Shannon), and it represents an estimate of the size of the state‑space of chess.  It’s important to note that this is an approximation; the exact count of all legal positions has not been computed because it would require enumerating an enormous combinatorial space.  For comparison, the number of possible complete games of chess is estimated to be around **10¹²⁰**.
